zakat.claim_evidence: The official website and donation pages for the US-based Al Jazari Institute (Minneapolis, MN) do not explicitly mention accepting zakat donations. Information regarding zakat acceptance and specific zakat-eligible categories was found on a page associated with 'Ibn Al Jazari Institute® Birmingham UK' (jazari.co.uk/zakat), which is an international affiliate and not the specific US organization being evaluated. (Source: https://ibnaljazariinstitute.com/donations/)

strengths_deep_dive: The AL Jazari Institute demonstrates a specialized focus on capacity building through its <cite id="1">Islamic and Arabic studies programs</cite>. A key financial strength is its <cite id="1">low fundraising cost</cite>, which is significantly better than the common $0.25 threshold. This efficiency allows the organization to navigate a <cite id="2">recent revenue decline</cite> while maintaining its core services. Furthermore, the institute's ability to generate <cite id="2">nearly half of its revenue through program fees</cite> suggests that its educational content is highly valued by the community it serves.
rich_narrative.summary: Based in Texas, the AL Jazari Institute provides Islamic education and civic engagement programs for families and the community. The organization focuses on <cite id="1">Qur'anic Sciences, Islamic Sciences, and Arabic programs</cite> to build local capacity. In FY2024, the institute reported <cite id="2">total revenue of $2,330,141</cite>, which represented a <cite id="2">22% decline from the previous year</cite>. Financial operations are balanced between <cite id="2">$1,586,418 in contributions</cite> and <cite id="2">$1,389,723 in program service revenue</cite> from its educational offerings. The organization maintains a <cite id="1">program expense ratio of 68.6%</cite>, which falls below the 75% industry benchmark. While the institute successfully <cite id="1">verifies outcomes for its educational programs</cite>, it currently <cite id="1">lacks a documented theory of change</cite> to map its long-term social impact. Fundraising remains efficient, costing only <cite id="1">$0.09 to raise every $1</cite> in donations. Governance is managed by a <cite id="1">100% independent board</cite>, though the board size is relatively small with only <cite id="1">four members</cite>.
